title: Investigate model internals
problem: You can access model weights and intermediate activations.
rationale: Use TransformerLens or NNsight for supported activation access; add SAELens when sparse-autoencoder analysis answers a concrete question.
first_step: Reproduce one known intervention and include a negative control before proposing a new explanation.
validation: Test intervention specificity, seed sensitivity, model coverage and out-of-distribution effects.
caveat: Attractive feature visualizations or activation correlations do not by themselves establish a causal mechanism.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Create a native-resolution image dataset
problem: A curated image task with exact dimensions, provenance and duplicate constraints.
rationale: Pillow and NumPy provide exact pixel control; Label Studio supports human review; DVC can track dataset revisions outside Git.
first_step: Define the schema and validation rules first; preserve raw sources and separate human-origin from synthetic records.
validation: Check dimensions, decode validity, hashes, split leakage, provenance and task-relevant human judgments.
caveat: A large dataset with weak provenance or near-duplicate leakage can be less useful than a smaller trusted set.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Build an interruptible voice assistant
problem: Low-latency speech interaction with live turns and interruptions.
rationale: Choose hosted or local speech recognition and synthesis separately; LiveKit coordinates real-time audio, while VAD detects speech boundaries.
first_step: Start with one language, a transcript-only prototype and a measurable end-of-turn policy.
validation: Measure end-to-end turn latency, interruption handling, recognition error and intelligibility in realistic noise.
caveat: Provider retention, voice rights, speaker consent and local hardware constraints require explicit choices.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Scale training beyond one accelerator
problem: A measured model-memory or training-time bottleneck.
rationale: Use DDP when a full replica fits; consider sharding when state does not fit; use tensor/pipeline parallelism only when the model and scale justify it.
first_step: Profile a correct single-device baseline, then validate a small multi-device run and checkpoint recovery.
validation: Measure useful samples/tokens per second, communication overhead, convergence parity and restart reliability.
caveat: Distributed complexity can erase speed gains; do not stack mutually overlapping engines without a deliberate design.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Track reproducible experiments
problem: You need to compare runs and recover exactly what produced a model.
rationale: Use a locked environment, versioned code/configuration, dataset identity and one tracking system.
first_step: Log parameters, dependency lock, code commit, data hashes and evaluation artifacts for a small experiment.
validation: Reproduce a result in a fresh environment without relying on undeclared local files.
caveat: Tracking metrics is not enough if the actual data, preprocessing or checkpoint is missing.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested
